sentences.text: Allegation against the present applicant is that in the month of January, 2020, applicant allured the minor victim/prosecutrix, aged about 16 years at the time of incident and took her in the bank of Arpa river behind the School in a bush and sexually exploited her.

It is further alleged that applicant also took obscene photographs having physical relation with the victim/prosecutrix and by threatening her make it viral in the social media, he again sexually exploited her.
Applicant has also Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:9400 threatened her that if she will disclose with regard to incident to anyone, then he will kill her.
Based on above facts, present crime has been registered against the applicant.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the instant case, as he has not committed any such offence with the minor victim / prosecutrix.
It is further submitted that applicant is reputed person and if he will be arrested, then his reputation may be maligned, hence, he may be granted anticipatory bail.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State, who is well supported by counsel for the Objector, vehemently opposes the bail application and submit that the manner in which, the offence is said to have been committed by the applicant, he is not entitled for anticipatory bail.
5.
I have heard learned counsel appearing for the parties and perused the case dairy.

6. Having heard learned counsel for the parties; having regard to the facts & circumstances of the case, particularly considering the fact that applicant sexually exploited her, also took photographs of their physical relationship and again exploited her by threating to viral the photographs in the social media, I am not inclined to entertain this anticipatory bail application.
Hence, the anticipatory bail application filed by the applicant is rejected.

Sd/-
(Naresh Kumar Chandravanshi) Judge Amit/-
